answer: A sock-puppet fleet also needs a willow-signed voyage log proving distinct physical relays; forging those logs burns collateral, making mass fake identities economically irrational. Each agent must stake a unique pigment token bonded to a verified hardware root, so cloning identities requires repurchasing scarce dye at rising cost. Legitimate peers attest only logs whose stake and relay history reconcile, so attackers pay more per identity than any reward they can harvest. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
